title: Grow facility licence intake
notes: One question asks for one fact. Do not combine facts in one answer.
Speak the answer in full sentences. Say names, numbers and units clearly.
If the answer is not known, say 'not known' and say who knows it.
Take a photo of each document or item that the question names.

routes.amend: Add or change a location on a current licence

questions.q: Who does this interview?
Who gives the answers? Give the full name and the role.
Which type of application do you need?
questions.help: new = no licence now. amend = add or change a location. renew = the licence expires soon. other = change of responsible person, activity or security.

questions.q: Does the customer agree that we keep these answers and use them to prepare the application?
By which date must the application go to the Agency? Say why that date.
What is the full legal name of the company, as on the Companies Office register?
What is the company number?
What is the NZBN?
What is the registered office address?
Who holds the shares? Give each name and the number of shares.
questions.help: The Agency checks every person with significant influence. A trust or a parent company needs the names behind it.

questions.q: Who are the directors? Give each full name.
Does the industry code on the Companies Office register match medicinal cannabis cultivation?
questions.help: A wrong code is a small fix. Do it before you lodge.

questions.q: What is the company website and social media? Does any page sell or advertise seeds, clones or flower?
questions.help: The Agency looks at public pages. Claims about past illegal growing, seed sales or 'signed offtake' cause questions.

questions.q: What is the full legal name of the responsible person, exactly as on the driver licence or passport?
questions.help: The Ministry of Justice check fails if the name does not match the ID. Include all middle names.
questions.photo: Front of the driver licence or passport

questions.q: What name does this person use every day?
What is the position of this person in the company?
What is the mobile phone number of this person?
What is the email address of this person? Is it a Google account?
questions.help: Shared Drive folders need a Google account. Record a second address if the main address is not a Google account.

questions.q: In which town or suburb does this person live?
How many minutes does this person need to drive from home to the site?
questions.help: The security plan must give a real alarm response time.

questions.q: Does this person have a criminal conviction or a pending charge, in New Zealand or in another country?
questions.help: Say 'none' if none. Do not guess. The Agency gets the record from the Ministry of Justice.

questions.q: Is there a second key-holder who lives near the site? Give the name, phone and drive time.
What is the licence number?
questions.photo: Every page of the current licence

questions.q: What is the expiry date on the licence?
questions.help: One licence has one expiry. A location added later expires on the same date.

questions.q: Which activities does the licence permit? For example cultivation, possession for manufacture, research.
Does the licence have conditions? Read each condition.
What are the addresses of all locations on the licence now?
Does each current location stay on the licence?
questions.help: You cannot move a location. You add the new location, then remove the old location.

questions.q: At each current location, which SOP version, register and electronic record system do you use today?
questions.help: If something changed at a current location without approval, stop and get advice before you lodge.

questions.q: Did you send every monthly supply return and the last 31 December stocktake? Give the date of the last one.
Is any record, manifest or register entry wrong or incomplete? Describe it.
questions.help: Never change a used record. We write a signed and dated correction note.

questions.q: What is the street address of the site?
What is the legal description? For example Lot 1 DP 123456.
questions.help: It is on the record of title or the council rates notice.

questions.q: What is the GPS position of the centre of the grow buildings?
questions.help: Use the GPS button while you stand at the buildings.

questions.q: What is the land area of the lot in square metres?
Who is the registered owner on the record of title?
questions.help: The owner must give written consent. We buy the title from LINZ to check the name.

questions.q: Does the company own the land, or does it lease the land?
Who is the landlord? Give the legal name, the person who can sign for the landlord, the phone and the email.
questions.photo: Lease, first page and signature page

questions.q: Does the lease cover the whole lot, or only part of the lot? Describe the leased part.
questions.help: Recommended: make the licensed area only the fenced grow compound. A small fenced area is easier to secure and to show on the plan.

questions.q: Who else uses the property? Is there a house on the lot? How do those people get in?
Do members of the public visit any part of the property?
What was the property used for before?
How far is the nearest house from the grow buildings, in metres?
questions.help: Some SOPs ask for 120 m. Closer houses need a strong odour and visibility plan.

questions.q: Are there easements, pipelines, power lines or drains on the lot? Where?
questions.help: Do a beforeUdig request before any post hole.

questions.q: Did the council say whether the buildings or containers need a building consent or a resource consent? Do you have it in writing?
How many vehicle entrances does the property have? Where is each one?
questions.help: Every entrance needs a locked gate. Only one entrance stays in use.

questions.q: List every building, room or container on the site. For each one, give a short name, for example C1 or Room 1.
questions.help: Use the site layout tool to draw each one to size. Include sheds and containers that hold no cannabis.

questions.q: For each one, give the internal length and the internal width in metres.
For each one, say what it is used for: flowering, vegetative, mothers, propagation, drying, storage, office or other.
Which building is the secure store for dried cannabis, seed and the register?
Is there a safe? Give the make, the model, the size and how it is fixed to the floor.
For each building, how do you go in? List each door in order, for example outer door, vestibule, inner door.
Does any door, window or vent have glass, or a weak panel?
How many rack tiers does each grow room have? What is the total bench area?
Where do you keep cannabis waste, and how do you destroy it?
Where is the quarantine area for new plants? Where is the breeding area, if any?
Are there more buildings or a greenhouse planned for later? Where, and what size?
questions.help: Leave future stages out of this application. Add them later with a separate amendment.

questions.q: Take photos of each building from outside, each door and each room inside. Say what each photo shows.
Is all cultivation indoors? If not, give the outdoor area in square metres.
What is the total indoor cultivation area in square metres? Do not include drying or storage rooms.
How do you control the climate? Name the air conditioning, the dehumidifiers and the controller.
Do you inject CO2? If yes, where are the bottles and is there a CO2 alarm?
What is the most plants you will have at one time, in each stage?
List every cultivar you hold now. For each one, say where it came from.
questions.help: Each name must be in the register and the last stocktake. Keep one provenance sheet for each cultivar.

questions.q: Do you want to declare a new New Zealand variety? Give its name.
questions.help: Each variety needs its own Form D and fee.

questions.q: Which pesticides or fertilisers do you use? Do you keep a spray log?
What is the largest quantity of dried cannabis you will hold on site at one time, in kilograms? How soon do you send it after cure?
Describe the fence around the licensed area: type, height, and any gaps.
questions.help: Recommended: a continuous, climb-resistant fence at least 1.8 m high, with a ground gap of no more than 120 mm. Plain chain-link usually fails.
questions.photo: Each run of fence and each gate

questions.q: Is there an electric fence? Who installed it, is it live, and is there a certificate to AS/NZS 3016?
How does the entrance gate lock? Is there a keypad or a fob?
Which door locks are on each building? Give the make and model if known. Do they need two factors, for example PIN and fob?
Is there an intruder alarm? Who installed it, and what is the installer's security technician licence number?
questions.help: The installer must hold a licence under the Private Security Personnel and Private Investigators Act 2010.

questions.q: What is the exact legal name of the alarm monitoring company? Is the contract signed? Is there patrol response?
questions.help: Check the name on the contract. A name we cannot find causes an information request.

questions.q: How many cameras are there now? Are they wired or battery? Where does each one point?
questions.help: Use wired cameras only. Put a camera inside each room and at each point of entry.

questions.q: Where is the camera recorder? How many days does it keep the video? Is it on a UPS?
questions.help: Recommended: at least 30 days of storage and at least 60 minutes of UPS.

questions.q: Are there duress buttons? Where?
Is there outside security lighting? Where?
Which security items are not installed yet? For each item, give the supplier and the date it will be done.
questions.help: The Agency inspects only a finished site. Get written quotes.

questions.q: Did you tell the local police about the site? Give the reference number.
Is a carbon filter fitted on every exhaust now? If not, when?
Do the rooms run under negative pressure?
How often do you change the carbon filters?
Did any neighbour complain about odour, noise or light? What did you do?
How many staff work on site? Give the name and role of each person who can witness a receipt or a destruction.
Who does a person working alone call to check in?
Do you keep a bound paper register? Where is it kept?
Which electronic record system do you use? Give the product, the version, where the data is hosted and who owns the account.
questions.help: Take a screenshot of the batch screen and the audit log.
questions.photo: Screenshot of the batch screen and audit log

questions.q: How do you transport cannabis? Who drives, and is there a manifest and an escort?
To whom will you supply the crop? Give the company name.
questions.help: The Agency returns an application that does not show where the crop goes.

questions.q: What is the buyer's licence number? Does the buyer's licence include possession for manufacture?
questions.help: Get a copy of the buyer's licence.

questions.q: Is a supply agreement signed? If not, is a letter of intent signed? Give the date.
Who at the buyer signs the agreement? Give the name, phone and email.
Do you have other supply agreements, current or old? Do they continue?
questions.help: An old agreement continues until you end it by notice.

questions.q: Will you supply plants or seed to other licence holders?
Will you export, or send samples to a lab overseas?
Will you do breeding or research? Give the maximum seedlings, breeding plants and mother plants each year.
questions.help: Give upper limits you will stay under.

questions.q: For each location, does the owner's written permission cover the renewed licence period? Give the date of the last letter.
Did the security, SOPs or records change at any location since the last approval?
Did the supply purposes change since the last approval?
Does the customer know the Agency fees and agree to pay each invoice on the day it arrives?
questions.help: The assessment starts only after payment.

questions.q: When will the build be finished and tested? Is that date realistic?
Is any cannabis at the new site now, or was it ever there?
questions.help: If yes, stop. Get legal advice before you lodge.

questions.q: Who is a JP near the customer, and when can the customer see the JP?
Is there anything else we must know?
Take a photo of each document you have: licence, ID, title, lease, landlord letter, supply agreement, quotes, certificates.
Draw the site layout. Put each building, the fence, the gates and north.
questions.help: Draw each building to size. Drag to move. Tap 'Turn' to turn it 90 degrees.

questions.q: Make a quick sketch of anything the layout tool cannot show.
